title: Creamy leek and cheddar pasta with crispy crumbs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Butter, leeks, garlic, dried pasta, frozen peas, crème fraîche, cheddar, breadcrumbs and olive oil are all ordinary home ingredients.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream UK supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a large pan, a frying pan and a grater, and uses simple techniques.

works.reason: 350g pasta with 3 leeks, 150g peas, 150g crème fraîche and 100g cheddar, loosened with pasta water, makes a properly sauced dish for four, and the frying pan is free for the crumbs once the leeks are tipped out.

honest_times.reason: Twenty active minutes covers washing and slicing the leeks, grating, zesting, softening the leeks and frying the crumbs, and 12 minutes matches boiling the penne.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used in the steps, penne is a fair name for dried pasta, and nothing unlisted appears apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: A warm, creamy leek pasta suits early February, and the three leeks are the heart of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are short, clear and in plain British English, with no restaurant language.

hearty_healthy.reason: It is a filling family lunch with plenty of leeks and peas alongside the pasta and cheese.
